worked_solution:
The function 

$$
f(x,y,z)=\sqrt{x-y+z}
$$

is continuous except when the expression under the radical is negative. However, the point $(3,1,-1)$ does not cause the  expression under the radical  to be negative, so we can calculate the limit by substituting  $(-3,1,-1)$ into the function: 

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to (3,1,-1)}\sqrt{x-y+z} & =\sqrt{3-1+(-1)} \\  & =\sqrt{3-1-1} \\  & =\sqrt{1} \\  & =1\end{aligned}
$$
